heading: Chap. v.—Refutation of the previously mentioned errors.
paragraphs:
And that He Himself is not God over all, and the Father,
but His Son, He [shows when He] says, “I ascend unto my
Father and your Father, and to my God and your God.”[1830]
And again, “When all things shall be subdued unto Him,
then shall He also Himself be subject unto Him that put all
things under Him, that God may be all in all.”[1831] Wherefore
it is one [Person] who put all things under, and who is all
in all, and another [Person] to whom they were subdued,
who also Himself, along with all other things, becomes subject
[to the former].
